title: ʻOkina & Kahakō
description: Train accurate Hawaiian spelling through noticing, handwriting, and retrieval after the model is hidden.

activities.support: Restore the missing Hawaiian orthography without looking anything up.
activities.explanation: ʻAʻole contains two ʻokina: one at the beginning and one between A and o. There is no kahakō in this word.

activities.instruction: Study the word, then hide it and produce it from memory.
activities.prompt: Learn the spelling, not the shape.
activities.support: Notice the exact placement of each mark before you hide the model.
studyNotes: Two ʻokina: one at the beginning and one between A and o
Say the word aloud while you study it
activities.paperInstruction: Write the word you just studied three times on paper from memory. Say it aloud each time. Then type it from memory.
activities.explanation: You retrieved the spelling after the model disappeared. The key detail is remembering both ʻokina and not adding a kahakō.
The ʻokina in Hawaiʻi comes before the final i and belongs in the spelling.

activities.prompt: Pay attention to exactly where the ʻokina occurs.
activities.support: Notice the spelling before the model is hidden.
studyNotes: One ʻokina before the final i
Say the syllables slowly while you study it
activities.paperInstruction: Write the word you just studied three times on paper from memory. Then type it from memory.
activities.explanation: The goal is to retrieve the location of the ʻokina, not simply recognize it when it is shown.

activities.support: Restore all missing ʻokina and kahakō.
activities.explanation: ʻŌlelo begins with an ʻokina and Ō with a kahakō. Hawaiʻi contains an ʻokina before the final i.

activities.instruction: Study the phrase, hide it, then rebuild it from memory.
activities.prompt: This time you must remember more than one orthographic mark.
activities.support: Notice the exact marks in each word before hiding the phrase.
studyNotes: Hawaiʻi has an ʻokina before the final i
Only ʻŌlelo contains a kahakō in this phrase
activities.paperInstruction: Write the phrase you just studied three times on paper from memory. Circle each ʻokina and underline each kahakō from memory. Then type the phrase from memory.
activities.explanation: Combining handwriting, speaking, and delayed typing forces you to reconstruct the spelling instead of copying it.

activities.instruction: Produce the Hawaiian spelling from meaning alone.
activities.explanation: Even a short word must be retrieved with its initial ʻokina.
